_comentario: First Numbers, Part 3 (spring, days 131-195): the English text of each day of Aprendo los números (content/q3.json). Day 174 is one of the two days whose activity differs from the Spanish book: 'Number names' (13 and 30, 14 and 40, 15 and 50), because in English they sound almost the same -- see notes/02-english.md.

dias.frase: Toby runs off across the park, and disappears behind five bushes.
Lucía and Dani look for Toby, and on the path they see four paw prints.
Lucía whistles Toby's song seven times, and they hear a bark.
Dad gets Toby out from between the rocks, and they all give him eight hugs.
From that day on, Toby has a new lead with ten stars on it.
checklist: I can add with pictures.
I know what the + sign means.
I know that 5 + 5 = 10.
dias.prompt: Draw the whole family hugging Toby.

dias.frase: Dani eats five pieces of apple, and feels a tooth wobbling.
That night his tooth comes out, and Dani looks at his top teeth: he has six left.
Lucía tells him that a little mouse brought her three coins for her teeth.
Dani puts his coin in his piggy bank, with seven more: now he has eight!
Grandma tells them that she lost twenty baby teeth.
checklist: I can split a number in two.
I know that 5 is 2 and 3.
I know that 8 is 7 and 1.
dias.prompt: Draw Dani with his new coin.

dias.frase: Every child brings a book from home, and there are already three on Lucía's table.
At the library, Lucía sees a new bookcase with six stars painted on it.
The librarian shows Lucía two easy storybooks, with pictures.
Lucía wraps up the book for Dani, and sticks five hearts on it.
Dani opens the book carefully, and they read one page together.
checklist: I know how many more make 10.
I know that 7 and 3 make 10.
I know the pairs that make 10.

dias.frase: Grandma Rosa brings seven loaves from the day before, to make torrijas.
They dip the bread in milk with cinnamon, and Grandma fries four torrijas.
The whole kitchen smells of cinnamon, and there are already six torrijas on the plate.
Dani eats so many torrijas that there are only three left on the plate.
On Sunday, Lucía writes down the recipe: milk, bread, cinnamon and two eggs.
checklist: I can take away, and count the ones that are left.
I know what the − sign means.
I know that 8 − 5 = 3.
dias.prompt: Draw Grandma's kitchen, smelling of cinnamon.

dias.frase: Seven carrots are growing in the school's new vegetable garden.
dias.texto: There are 9 carrots in the garden, and Lucía pulls up 2. How many are left in the ground?

dias.frase: Lucía moves her bean plant to a bigger pot, and it already has five leaves.
dias.texto: Lucía has 3 plants in her pot, and Marta gives her 2 more. How many has she got now?

dias.frase: Every morning, the children water the garden with eight watering cans.
Each child puts in a stick with their name on it, and Dani counts six tomatoes.
dias.texto: There are 4 red tomatoes and 2 green ones on the plant. How many tomatoes are there?

dias.frase: On Friday, Lucía takes three tomatoes home from the garden.
checklist: I can take away with pictures.
I can listen to a problem and do the calculation.
I know when to add and when to take away.
dias.prompt: Draw the school vegetable garden, with its plants.

dias.frase: Dad takes off the stabilisers, and Lucía's bike is left with two wheels.
There are four bikes parked in the park, and one of them is Lucía's.
Lucía, Sofía and Dani go for a ride: three bikes round the park.
Toby runs beside the bike, and leaves ten paw prints in the sand.
Dad gives Lucía one shiny new bell for her bike.
checklist: I can count in twos.
I know that 2 bikes have 4 wheels.
I can add up to 10.
dias.prompt: Draw Lucía riding her bike, without stabilisers.

dias.frase: There are five fish painted on the wall of the swimming pool.
In the swimming lesson, three children put their hands up.
Javier, the teacher, puts fifteen stars on the pool noticeboard.
Lucía and Sofía splash in the water with their four hands.
Lucía can swim on her own now, and Javier gives her one star sticker.
checklist: I can count in fives.
I know that two hands have 10 fingers.
I can count to 20 in fives.
dias.prompt: Draw Lucía swimming in the pool.

dias.frase: Lucía and Dani make Mum a present with four hearts on it.
Dad helps them buy five flowers for Mum.
On Sunday, Mum has breakfast in bed with nine biscuits.
dias.texto: Dad puts 6 biscuits on the tray, and Dani puts 3 more. How many biscuits are there?

dias.frase: Mum says it is the nicest present ever, and gives them eight kisses.
In the afternoon, they eat in Grandma's garden: six plates on the table.
checklist: I can add up to 10.
I can take away up to 10.
I can do a word problem.
dias.prompt: Draw a present for someone you love very much.

dias.frase: Dani plays letters with Lucía, and he already gets thirty cards right.
Lucía shows him forty cards, one after another.
Dani sounds out the letters of a storybook with fifty pages.
Dad tells Dani he is going to be a great reader, and gives him thirty kisses.
Lucía thinks that soon they will read together: forty stories!
checklist: I can count in tens, up to 50.
I know that 30 is 3 tens.
I can tell thirteen from thirty.
dias.prompt: Draw Dani reading his first story.

dias.frase: Marta announces the end-of-year party: it is twenty-nine days away.
Sofía and Lucía practise a dance with twenty-three steps.
Dani will open the party, in front of twenty-one classmates.
Mum is going to make her chocolate cake for twenty-seven children.
There is only one week to go, and Lucía has practised twenty-two times.
checklist: I know the numbers from 21 to 29.
I know that 23 is 2 tens and 3 ones.
I can count to 30.

dias.frase: The class is looking after a caterpillar, and they have changed its leaves thirty-four times.
Lucía looks at the caterpillar's jar thirty-one times.
Marta says that some butterflies live for thirty-six days.
An orange and black butterfly comes out, and Lucía counts thirty-eight spots on it.
The butterfly flies away, and Lucía counts to thirty-nine.
checklist: I know the numbers from 31 to 39.
I know how many tens a number has.
I can put numbers up to 40 in order.
dias.prompt: Draw the caterpillar, and the butterfly it turns into.

dias.frase: At the book fair there are forty-five storybooks on the table.
Lucía helps Dani choose a storybook with forty-two pages.
Lucía works out that it would take her forty-eight years to read them all.
Each classmate tells their story: forty-four minutes altogether.
That night, Lucía reads Dani forty-nine pages.
checklist: I know the numbers from 41 to 49.
I know that 45 is 4 tens and 5 ones.
I can count to 50.
dias.prompt: Draw your favourite story, and yourself reading it.

dias.frase: Today is the last day of school, and there are ten balloons in the classroom.
Marta hands out the reports, and a diploma to each of the twenty children.
On the way home, Lucía thinks about everything she has learnt: fifty things!
Mum shows them a photo of Lucía from one year ago.
dias.texto: One year ago, Lucía was 6. Now she is 7. How many years older is she?

dias.frase: That night they have dinner in Grandma Rosa's garden, under forty stars.
checklist: I can add and take away up to 10.
I know the numbers up to 50.
I can count in twos, fives and tens.
dias.prompt: Draw what you liked best about this school year.
